final_answer:
DEVIATION REPORT - CASCADE ENVIRONMENTAL SOLUTIONS, INC. $285M SENIOR SECURED CREDIT FACILITY
Prepared for: Hargrove, Pennington & Locke LLP (Borrower's counsel; R. Thayer / D. Ochoa). Compared: Caldwell Strauss & Moran draft Credit Agreement dated April 18, 2025 (CA) against the executed Term Sheet dated March 14, 2025 (TS). Privileged and confidential; attorney work product.

1. BOTTOM LINE
Lender's counsel's transmittal (Apr. 18) calls the changes "administrative and mechanical." They are not. We found 40+ deviations, nearly all adverse to Borrower, many of which change the economics, covenant headroom or default risk. Several TS terms are simply missing (equity cure, revolver pricing Level 3, ECF threshold and voluntary-prepayment credit, SunGard limits, MAE carve-outs). Comments are requested by about May 2, 2025 for a May 30 closing (TS Outside Date June 30, 2025). The email also states that credit committee approval is conditioned on terms "not materially less favorable to the Lenders than those reflected in this draft"; that is a negotiating position, not a TS term, and should be rejected in writing.

2. LEGAL FRAMEWORK AND LEVERAGE
- The TS is expressly non-binding except confidentiality, exclusivity, expenses and governing law, and says the definitive Credit Agreement controls on conflict (TS s.16). CA s.10.10 is an integration clause superseding prior understandings. Once signed, the TS gives no protection; every deviation must be fixed in the draft.
- Under New York law (TS s.16; CA s.10.13), a preliminary agreement can bind parties to negotiate open terms in good faith within the agreed framework (Type II): Teachers Ins. & Annuity Ass'n v. Tribune Co., 670 F. Supp. 491 (S.D.N.Y. 1987); Brown v. Cara, 420 F.3d 148 (2d Cir. 2005) (verified, holding enforceable obligation to negotiate in good faith, not the ultimate deal). The TS specifies economics and a detailed framework while saying definitive terms are "subject to negotiation" and "satisfactory to all parties" and omitting any express good-faith covenant; a Type II argument is available but uncertain, and a damages remedy is hard to quantify. Use it as leverage (pointing to unilateral retrades of agreed terms), not as a litigation plan. TS exclusivity runs to May 30, 2025, so Borrower cannot shop the deal; time pressure favors Lenders, so prioritize.
- Approach: present a TS-conformity markup. Frame Tier 1 items as "restoring agreed terms," which is hard for the Agent to resist, and reserve trade-offs for Tier 3 items that the TS left open.

3. TIER 1 - CRITICAL (economic or default-risk; contradict express TS terms)
1. Equity cure deleted. TS s.11.4 gives Sponsor a cure (15 BD after Compliance Certificate; 2 per four quarters, 4 over life; no consecutive quarters; cure amount added to Adjusted EBITDA). CA has none; s.8.01(b) makes any s.7.11 breach an immediate no-cure Event of Default. Restore s.11.4 verbatim (new s.7.11(d) plus a carve-out in s.8.01(b)); also add a standstill on remedies during the cure period.
2. DDTL availability cut from 18 to 12 months (CA s.1.01 Availability Period; s.2.03(d); s.3.02(d)). TS s.3.3: through Nov. 30, 2026. CA: May 30, 2026. Draw mechanics tightened: max 3 draws, $10M minimum (TS: unlimited draws, $5M minimum). Practical effect: $50M acquisition capacity may lapse before the integration or sourcing window, while the 0.50% ticking fee runs on undrawn amounts. Restore date, draws and minimum.
3. SOFR floor raised from 0.75% to 1.00% (definition of SOFR; ss.1.06(b), 2.08). The floor was also embedded into the definition of SOFR itself, so it leaks into the Base Rate (SOFR+1.00%) and benchmark replacement. Worth up to 25 bps (about $0.6M per year on a fully drawn $235M term debt) when rates sit below the floor. Restore 0.75% and relocate floor to the interest provisions only. Also, CA "SOFR" is the overnight NY Fed rate, but TS and the 1/3/6-month Interest Periods require Term SOFR; define Term SOFR (CME) and keep any credit spread adjustment at zero. The email's description of "hardwired" benchmark replacement is inaccurate: s.1.06 is an amend-with-negative-consent mechanic.
4. Revolver pricing grid: Level 3 (SOFR+3.25% below 3.00x) omitted; only two levels (s.2.08(a); Exhibit D). Margin step-down effective on the fifth Business Day (TS: first Business Day after certificate). Restore three-tier grid and timing.
5. Capex covenant: cap cut from $12.0M to $10.5M (s.7.10; TS s.9.4), carry-forward (25% of unused, one year) and partial-year proration deleted, and "Capital Expenditures" counts financed spend (definition). Cost to Borrower: a 12.5% lower cap and loss of up to $3.0M of flexibility each year. Restore TS terms.
6. Total Net Leverage Ratio inputs tightened. (a) Cash netting cap $10M vs. TS $15M (Total Net Leverage definition; s.7.11(a)); at closing, (185-10)/42.6 = 4.11x versus TS 4.01x. Also narrowed to cash under Control Agreements and excluding foreign cash and LC cash collateral, though DACAs are not due until 60 days post-closing (Sched. 5.12). (b) Adjusted EBITDA omits TS add-backs for non-recurring and cash restructuring charges; limits transaction-cost add-back to 12 months post-closing and non-Acquisition items; nets realized synergies; requires "factually supportable" certification. Lower EBITDA directly shrinks headroom against 4.75x/1.20x tests and the ECF grid. Restore TS definitions.
7. Material Adverse Effect and closing conditionality. TS s.6(e) uses the Acquisition Agreement MAE and promised customary carve-outs and SunGard limited conditionality (s.6(n)). CA defines MAE with no carve-outs (general economic/industry conditions, changes in law/GAAP, etc.) and adds prongs for Loan Party performance and Lenders' rights. CA s.3.01(e)/(q) require all representations true at closing, with no Specified Representations/Specified Defaults limit. Also added: three years of audits, local counsel opinions, pending-litigation searches, satisfactory lien searches, 4.75x test, and waiver only by Agent and Required Lenders. Closing certainty is the Sponsor's key risk; insist on SunGard language and Acquisition-Agreement MAE for the closing condition.
8. Change of Control (definition; s.8.01(j)). Threshold 50.1% (TS 50%); Fund-only "and Affiliates" (TS includes co-investors and related funds); new key-man trigger (David Whitmore ceasing to be "actively involved"), contrary to TS statement that the definition is "limited to ownership threshold and structural control provisions." Delete (d); restore 50% and co-investor language. (Clause (c) limited to Subordinated Indebtedness is narrower than TS and favorable.)
9. Excess Cash Flow sweep (s.2.05(b)(i); definition). Omitted: $2.0M gross minimum threshold; dollar-for-dollar credit for voluntary prepayments; deduction for cash Permitted Acquisition consideration. Added: $3.0M lifetime cap on restructuring deduction. Restore all three TS terms; the sweep (25%/50%) compounds with the higher leverage calculation in item 6.
10. Permitted Acquisitions (definition; DDTL use). Individual cap $20M (TS $25M); 15 Business Days' prior notice (TS 10 with pro forma certificate; shorter allowed); new quality-of-earnings report above $10M; no Required Lender consent route for above-cap deals. Restore $25M and 10 BD; delete QoE or raise to $20M.
11. Guarantors/collateral. CA requires all Subsidiaries as Guarantors with no excluded subsidiary, immaterial-subsidiary (<5% assets), foreign (65% pledge) or unrestricted subsidiary carve-outs; "Collateral" has no excluded assets (permits, licenses, titled vehicles, leaseholds that cannot lawfully be pledged), a real concern for a permitted waste/remediation business. Restore TS exceptions and add customary Excluded Assets.
12. Events of Default tightened: (a) interest/fee grace 3 BD (TS 5 BD); (b) judgment default 30 days (TS 60); (c) cross-default triggers on mere right to accelerate and counts undrawn commitments (TS requires acceleration or payment failure at maturity, $2.5M); (d) new environmental EoD (s.8.01(k)) not in TS; (e) Default Rate applies to all Obligations from date of EoD (TS: overdue amounts). Conform to TS.

4. TIER 2 - SIGNIFICANT
13. Management fee cap $1.0M (TS $1.5M); TS permits accrual/subordination during default, CA prohibits payment (s.7.06(b)). Restore $1.5M; accrual rights.
14. Annual audited financials due in 90 days (TS 120, s.5.01(a)); going-concern carve-out for final-year maturity removed. Restore.
15. Insurance proceeds reinvestment 180 days (TS 270); asset-sale reinvestment lacks the TS 180-day extension for committed reinvestments and imposes 10-BD notice (s.2.05(b)(ii),(iv)). Application of mandatory prepayments pro rata between TLA/DDTL (TS: TLA first, then DDTL). (Business-interruption proceeds exclusion is favorable.)
16. Fixed Charge Coverage: "Scheduled Debt Amortization" (definition) could capture the maturity balloon in the final test periods; TS refers to regular amortization. Clarify exclusion of balloon, voluntary and mandatory prepayments.
17. Fee Letter: TS s.17 describes a letter dated March 14 among Borrower, Sponsor and Agent; CA defines it as dated March 28 among Borrower, Holdings and Ridgeline, and makes it a Loan Document (guaranteed, secured, default-triggering). Confirm which exists; obtain the executed letter before signing; carve it out of Loan Documents for default purposes.
18. Indemnity/expenses (s.10.04): TS limits counsel to one primary plus local counsel and excludes bad-faith conduct; CA covers any counsel, claims brought by Borrower, "any Environmental Liability related in any way" to Borrower, and excludes only gross negligence/willful misconduct. Restore TS limits, add bad faith and material breach and disputes among Indemnitees carve-outs; limit environmental indemnity to Borrower-caused conditions during ownership.
19. Post-closing (s.5.12; Sched. 5.12): TS gives 90 days with extensions in Agent's reasonable discretion; CA uses 30/60/90/120 days (UCC and insurance at 30; DACAs 60) and failure is an EoD. Align to 90 days with extension right.
20. Disqualified Institutions protection (TS s.13(e)) is omitted from s.10.06; add DQ list mechanics. (TS permits no Borrower consent for assignments to Lenders/affiliates/Approved Funds; CA requires consent for all absent default, which favors Borrower.)
21. Amendment/voting: TS requires unanimous consent for lien subordination and amortization postponement; CA s.10.01 omits lien subordination and s.9.10(c) lets the Agent subordinate liens. Primarily lender-side but affects Borrower's collateral stability; low priority.
22. Notice and mechanics: Holdings guaranty keepwell is fine; Acquisition Agreement defined as an SPA dated March 14 with Holdings, Borrower and "sellers" - confirm against the actual agreement. Equity condition in s.3.01(i) and closing statement that the Borrower "has reported" LTM metrics (s.3.01(f)) should be factual recital only, not a condition.

5. TIER 3 - MINOR, CLARIFYING OR UNEXPECTED ADDITIONS
23. Incremental facility (s.2.14), up to $40M with MFN of 50 bps (lapses after six months). Not in TS; marketed as borrower-friendly. It is useful, but Agent-satisfaction conditions and sole-discretion Lender participation make it illusory; add a leverage-based free-and-clear capacity, MFN sunset on defined terms, and Agent consent only for technical terms. Do not trade TS economics for it.
24. Defaulting lender, benchmark replacement, 1/3/6-month periods, base rate options: customary; check the Benchmark Replacement Date definition (missing), and the Required Lender objection mechanic.
25. Basket detail left open by TS: purchase money $3M, liens general $2M, other debt $1M, investments $3M lifetime, employee repurchases $500K, other dispositions $500K, loans to employees $500K, affiliate transactions lack TS board-approval threshold. Negotiate upward; the TS expressly anticipates agreeing amounts.
26. Exclusive jurisdiction lists both NY Supreme (Manhattan) and SDNY equally; TS puts SDNY first. Governing law clause omits reference to GOL s.5-1401. Conform.
27. Notice details and signature blocks contain errors: emails (rthayer@hpllaw.com, pgranville@csmlaw.com, kfulton@ridgelinenational.com) differ from transmittal email domains; Holdings signatory is Thomas Elridge (VP) vs. TS David Whitmore; Agent signatory title differs. Correct. Sponsor is not a CA party; confirm intended.
28. Article VI is "reserved" although the transmittal references "information covenants (Article VI)"; reporting sits in Article V. Confirm no covenants were dropped.

6. DEVIATIONS FAVORABLE TO BORROWER (do not raise; confirm internally with client)
- Leverage covenant step-downs are one quarter later than TS (4.75x through June 30, 2026; 4.50x to Dec. 31, 2026; 4.25x to Dec. 31, 2027; 4.00x from March 31, 2028) (s.7.11(a)). TS: through March 31, 2026; June-Sept 2026; Dec 2026-Sept 2027; Dec 2027. Likely a drafting slip; no duty to flag, but do not rely on it, and expect correction. Advise client of risk the Lender frames any ask as a reason to refuse other TS fixes; do not misstate it. Caution: no affirmative misrepresentation about the schedule.
- No MAE Event of Default (TS s.12(l)); EoD (k) is narrower in some respects. ERISA threshold $5M. Voluntary prepayment inverse-order election. Business-interruption exclusion. Default Rate at Required Lender election (not automatic). Change of Control clause (c) narrower. Mandatory prepayments do not reduce Revolver commitments. Borrower consent to all assignments absent default.

7. RECOMMENDED APPROACH AND NEXT STEPS
1. Send a short cover note rejecting the "mechanical" characterization and the "not materially less favorable" condition; state that Borrower expects the CA to conform to the executed TS and that exclusivity assumes good-faith documentation.
2. Deliver a full markup within the May 2 target; open with a TS conformity table covering Tier 1 items 1-12 and require Agent response before negotiating Tier 3.
3. Priorities: (a) equity cure, (b) SunGard/MAE, (c) DDTL window, (d) covenant definitions (cash cap, Adjusted EBITDA, capex), (e) pricing/floor/Term SOFR, (f) Change of Control, (g) ECF.
4. Model covenant headroom (4.75x test, 1.20x FCCR, $10M liquidity) using both CA and TS definitions with the Sponsor's financial advisor (Trellis) and the Borrower CFO; quantify items 3, 5, 6 and 9 for client sign-off.
5. Ask the Agent to produce a redline against the TS and the executed Fee Letter.
6. Calendar: closing May 30; TS Outside Date June 30; exclusivity ends May 30. Confirm timing status with the client if comments are late.

8. LIMITS
I reviewed only the CA draft, the TS (including exhibits) and the transmittal email; I did not see the Fee Letter, Acquisition Agreement, Sponsor model or schedules not in the draft. TS Section 13 text was read partially. Legal authority was limited to two NY cases; no jurisdiction-specific analysis of enforceability of the Type II claim has been done.
